description:
Fact, measured on fz-sc8/distill-fz at 864b7dbd1:

    def f(t) when tuple_size(t) == 0, do: :empty
    def f(_), do: :other
    def main(), do: dbg(f({}))

- interp: "fz2 interp: backend clause dispatch required omitted semantic input 0"
- run: error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan] "native clause dispatch required omitted semantic input 0 for executable 50"
- Elixir prints :empty.

The argument `{}` is zero-width, so its semantic input is omitted from the executable, but the guard still reads it. The dispatch plan and the omitted-input decision disagree about whether the guard is a reader. Found by the fz-sc8.9 builder; it predates fz-sc8.9 for any guard over a zero-width input.

Design (page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.31.html; APPROVED 2026-10-18):
- Root cause: prepare_runtime_demand_for_type (executable_facts.rs:505-535) projects a tuple type as tuple_fields(field demands); for {} (and any type whose every leaf is an empty tuple) normalized (semantic.rs:395-410) turns it into Ignore, so the input is dropped (artifact.rs:538-562) while the dispatch plan still reads it (pattern.rs:58, joined at runtime_demand.rs:1281-1292).
- Fix: one rule at the projection, for both dispatch and boundary: a value that is read is present; when the tuple's field demands all come out Ignore, the projection is Whole (always zero lanes there).
- normalized and the two loud refusals (native.rs:856-875, ir_interp/backend.rs:724-737) are unchanged.
- Tests: unit test in executable_facts' sibling _test.rs ({} and {{}} not Ignore, {1} unchanged); oracle fixture on all three paths ({}, {{}}, via a typed-head helper and tuple_size(t) == 0; {1} and 5 take the other clause).
- Predicted: no other fixture, pin or golden moves.
title: An entry guard that reads only an empty tuple fails to compile
